source.title: Unlearning Virus Knowledge Toward Safe and Responsible Mutation Effect Predictions
source.authors: Ming-Chen Li; Bingxin Zhou; Yang Tan; Liang Hong

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests virus-knowledge unlearning in protein language models, extending unlearning evaluation to a different model domain. It evaluates reduced viral mutation-effect prediction and non-virus performance, but not recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates viral and non-viral mutation-effect prediction after editing. It does not test fine-tuning as a recovery attack, activation ablation, quantization, or prompting. MLM perplexities, representation plots, parameter-difference analysis, and supervised AAV/GB1 fine-tuning are not recorded as recovery-attack results; the supervised tasks deliberately train on the target assay.
record.test_reason: The study applies unlearning to protein language models (ESM-2) and reports viral vs non-viral mutation-effect prediction after editing. This bears on version A's forgetting-while-retaining part in a new domain. It tests no recovery attacks, so B to E are untested, and F is not tested against the attacks.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors conclude ProEdit cuts viral mutation-effect prediction while keeping non-viral performance, and they call it effective unlearning. They also say the alternative methods lose non-viral performance.
record.recipe_differences: P RO E DIT edits protein language models using objectives for virus forgetting, non-virus retention, and virus-like non-virus preservation; the paper also compares four alternative unlearning strategies. It does not implement or evaluate the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that increasing retrieval parameter k from 1 to 5 slowly reduces non-virus performance and does not improve viral forgetting; it selects k = 1. The values are discussed in the text with Figure 5.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper does not state a chance-level reference for the mutation-effect correlation measure and does not evaluate recovery attacks. Individual assay results are supplied for 28 assays, while the benchmark description states 30 viral assays.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 is not separately extracted because its model/value alignment is ambiguous in the supplied flattened layout and overlaps with the clearer aggregate results in Table 3. Individual assay results are listed for the 28 assays in Appendix A.2, Table 4. Figure 5's k sweep is described qualitatively but not entered as separate rows. Supervised AAV/GB1 results are omitted because those tasks train deliberately on assay labels rather than evaluate a recovery attack.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge; no chance-level reference for ρ.
No relearning fine-tuning attack. The supervised AAV fine-tuning trains on the target assay itself.
No activation ablation or access-vs-deletion analysis.
ProEdit is not tested against the recovery attacks.

missing.what: Table 2 results, including supervised AAV (viral, ρ down to -0.16/-0.18) and GB1 (non-viral) after fine-tuning on the target assay
missing.versions: A (and arguably B as a fine-tuning probe)

record.verdict_notes: The AAV result is fine-tuning where ProEdit stays low at ρ of -0.18 after supervised training on viral data. That is loosely a recovery-resistance observation, which the reader omitted. It is not a standard relearning attack, though, since the MLP head is trained and the model is used as an encoder. It is arguably relevant to B/F, so researchers should check the text. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Tests viral mutation-effect prediction reduction and non-virus performance, but not whether simple attacks recover the knowledge. No chance-level reference is stated.
No recovery fine-tuning attack using unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples is tested.
No activation-direction ablation is tested, and the analysis does not establish that the method blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
No quantization recovery test is reported.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery test is reported.
P RO E DIT is not tested against the recovery attacks in the claim.

relationships.condition: ProEdit on ESM-2 650M and 150M, zero-shot ProteinGym aggregate, no attacks
relationships.reason: Viral ρ fell 0.238 to 0.073 (650M) and 0.135 to 0.083 (150M); non-virus ρ went 0.475 to 0.470 and 0.449 to 0.430 (r11, r12, r23, r24, with baselines r01, r02, r13, r14). Recovery was not tested.
relationships.display_finding: Viral correlations fell from 0.238 to 0.073 and 0.135 to 0.083, while nonviral correlations changed from 0.475 to 0.470 and 0.449 to 0.430, without recovery testing.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: ProEdit on ESM-2 650M and 150M, zero-shot ProteinGym aggregate, no attacks
source_check.reason: Table 3 values match the rows: targeted-subset rho falls to near zero (0.238 -> 0.073; 0.135 -> 0.083) while the retained subset is nearly kept (0.475 -> 0.470; 0.449 -> 0.430). Version A's attack-resistance part is untested, which per the rules is listed as untested, not limits_scope.

relationships.reason: Forgetting is uneven: some assays drop sharply, but ρ stays positive on the Tsuboyama stability assays (r34 0.471, r47 0.534, r51 0.450), and a few assays are not reduced (r25, r35, r36, r38).
relationships.display_finding: Some assays declined sharply, but Tsuboyama stability correlations remained 0.471, 0.534 and 0.450, and several assays showed no reduction.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Table 4 shows rho still 0.471 (r34), 0.534 (r47) and 0.450 (r51) after editing, so 'near chance' does not hold assay by assay: forgetting is incomplete, which qualifies version A rather than contradicting it. The four 'not reduced' assays (r25, r35, r36, r38) have near-zero baselines (0.071, 0.017, 0.020, 0.038) and add little weight to this verdict.

relation.reason: The paper's own Table 3 and Table 4 results bear on whether version A holds in this setting; it does not merely cite or assume it.

tranche.reason: Unlearning applied in a new setting (protein language models, zero-shot mutation-effect prediction) with its own result on version A's forget-while-retain part. Not T1/T2 (no original's method or measure), not T4 (reports results on the claim, not just its own tool).

source_check.notes: All 11 rows verified: Table 3 and Table 4 values, baselines, subjects and conditions match exactly. Not captured by the checked rows: the supervised fine-tuning results (Table 2, AAV and GB1) and the Figure 4(a) AAV validation curve, which also bear on version A's retention side; Table 2 reports the aggregates rounded (0.24 -> 0.08) while Table 3 gives 0.238 -> 0.073, and Table 2's AAV base value 0.35 conflicts with 0.34 in the text. Single run throughout, no seeds or intervals, and no attack, relearning or quantization test, so the record says nothing about versions B to F.

statements.correction: This study, from Table 3: ProEdit on ESM-2-650M, zero-shot ProteinGym aggregate Spearman rho, viral subset 0.238 -> 0.073, non-viral subset 0.475 -> 0.470; ESM-2-150M 0.135 -> 0.083 and 0.449 -> 0.430. Table 4, per-assay for ProEdit 650M: rho stays 0.471, 0.534, 0.450 on three Tsuboyama stability assays. No recovery attack, relearning or quantization test was run. Single run, no seeds or intervals. Provenance: bioRxiv preprint, code available, controls and capability check present, uncertainty absent.
statements.problem: The statement cites r11 but gives no number, model or method from this study: no protein language model, ESM-2 or ProEdit appears. Its enumerated non-LLM cases (image generation, image classes, speaker identity, toy autoencoder) and its 'why' provenance line (2410.08074, 2506.01318, 2507.20140, 2609.27593) both leave this study out. Its condition line, 'Results hold for specific methods and attacks', does not describe r11: this study ran no attack or relearning test at all, and within the same study the aggregate masks assays where the edited model keeps rho 0.45-0.53. No number it gives is from this study, so nothing it states about this study is false; it is incomplete rather than wrong.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: P RO E DIT, ProteinGym aggregate, zero-shot
reader_labels.reason: Viral Spearman’s ρ fell from 0.238 to 0.073 for 650M and from 0.135 to 0.083 for 150M, while non-virus scores changed from 0.475 to 0.470 and 0.449 to 0.430 (r01–r02, r11–r14, r23–r24). This supports suppression with non-virus performance largely maintained in the tested setting; recovery attacks were not tested.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Alternative unlearning methods on ProteinGym aggregate
reader_labels.reason: Results vary by model and method: some edits lowered viral prediction but also substantially degraded non-virus performance, and Gradient Ascent on 150M did not lower viral prediction (r03–r10, r15–r22).
